chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Edgar Hayes band's daily rehearsals; Harold Oxley and the road manager
summary: The band rehearsed every day at the Renaissance Casino unpaid, with Clarke borrowing nickels for meals; Oxley handled the band and sent Barkeley as road manager.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yeah, because -- I mean it -- this business of bands all going over all the time hadn't begun, had it?
No. But I'll tell you one thing. This band, Edgar Hayes, we had rehearsed every day for about a year, and when we weren't working we were rehearsing at the Renaissance Casino, every day.
Really.
Can you imagine that?
No.
No, I couldn't imagine it either.
(Laughter)

But we rehearsed -- we had to be on stage at the Renaissance Casino at 1:30 every day, and we would rehearse until we just became tired. No-one would say well -- look at their watch and say that's it. Never. We just

rehearsed and rehearsed. So when someone said, "Well, let's go out and have a Coke," and then we'd come back and we would start again, until like 6:00 or 7:00 o'clock at night, and someone would say, "Well, fellas, I'm tired," you know? So then we'd say we'd all go. Like the trumpet players, their lips became tired and so and so.
Yeah.
So we would kind of judge ourselves by them, because since they had the hardest job.
Yeah.
So when the trumpet players became tired then we would stop.
Then you'd all quit.
Now can you imagine, we rehearsed every day.
I think it's incredible.
It's incredible, huh?
You not only didn't -- I mean I suppose you weren't being paid for rehearsal.
No.
And you probably weren't even paying for the hall.
No. Mr. Andretti -- was it Andretti? He was the band leader, Adrian Andretti, but he had -- his good friend was running the Casino, the Renaissance, and he

-- Adrian told him, "Well, let Edgar Hayes and the boys rehearse, you know, they're trying to get together. Give them a break." And so it didn't cost us anything. But the only thing that really got me down was that I had to eat every day. So then I had to borrow nickels and dimes from the fellows in the band so that I could get a meal.
And keep your strength up.
(Laughter)
So we would work sometimes, which was very rare. Sometimes --
That's wonderful though, isn't it?
Sometimes -- that's why I say we haven't that --
Spirit.
-- spirit left. It doesn't exist anymore.
No.
And when we went to Europe, Harold said -- Harold Oxley said, "My God, you fellows are as good as Jimmy."
Did Harold send you too?
Huh?
Did he send the band?
Yeah, he was handling the band.
Fancy that. Did he go over with you?
No, he sent a fellow whose name was Barkeley.
Oh.
He went there with us as road manager. And his wife and Harold's daughter.
Oh, Harold's wife and daughter went?
No, his daughter went with the wife of Barkeley.
Oh, I see.
And the road manager, which his name was Barkeley.
Oh. Was he an American?
Yes, uh-huh.
Oh.
Yeah, they were from -- the Barkeleys were from Tennessee, if I'm not mistaken.
Oh.
